edges.description: Bacilli disseminate from the primary site through the bloodstream toward meningeal or subependymal foci.
A caseating focus at a meningeal or ependymal surface can rupture into the subarachnoid space.
Bacilli and antigens in CSF elicit dense granulomatous inflammation around the basal cisterns.
Basal exudate entraps and inflames adjacent cerebral arteries.
Dense exudate blocks basal subarachnoid cisterns and obstructs CSF flow.
Neutrophilic meningeal inflammation is accompanied by raised MMP-9 in cerebrospinal fluid.
The leukocytic meningeal inflammatory infiltrate is sampled as a lymphocyte-predominant CSF pleocytosis.
Basal exudate encases cranial nerve trunks crossing the basal cisterns, producing cranial nerve palsies, most often of the abducens nerve.
Inflammation of the meninges produces meningeal irritation, seen clinically as neck stiffness.
Meningeal inflammation produces the headache of the meningitic prodrome.
The granulomatous inflammatory response is accompanied by systemic fever.
Arteritic occlusion causes ischemic infarction in the supplied territory.
Infarction of the basal ganglia and internal capsule produces focal motor weakness, most often hemiparesis.
Late seizures in tuberculous meningitis are associated with cerebral infarction, as well as with tuberculoma and hyponatremia.
Ischemic brain injury contributes to the neurodisability seen in survivors, including cognitive impairment.
Obstructed CSF pathways produce clinically and radiologically apparent hydrocephalus.
Progressive hydrocephalus raises intracranial pressure, and patients deteriorate in consciousness until CSF is diverted.
Hydrocephalus and raised intracranial pressure contribute to brain injury and lasting neurodisability, including cognitive impairment.
MMP-9 degrades extracellular matrix around the blood-brain barrier. The causal step is shown in a mouse CNS-TB model, not in patients.
HIV infection increases the risk of active TB and CNS involvement among people with TB, but the cited sources do not pin the intervening steps to a single node in this graph.
Infected mice develop blood-brain barrier breakdown with MMP-9 secretion when SHH signalling is pharmacologically blocked.
edges.limitations: Barrier breakdown is produced under cyclopamine antagonism of SHH, an artificial accelerant with no counterpart in human TBM, in mice rather than humans; the basal exudate, arteritis and hydrocephalus are not reported.

nodes.description: Dexamethasone is recommended as adjunctive host-directed therapy and lowers early CSF MMP-9, but its survival benefit is modest and heterogeneous. A phase 3 trial in HIV-negative adults stratified by LTA4H genotype found no benefit over placebo in CC and CT genotypes and no better outcome in TT genotype, so genotype-guided steroid use is not established.

evidence.reference_title: Dexamethasone, cerebrospinal fluid matrix metalloproteinase concentrations and clinical outcomes in tuberculous meningitis.
evidence.snippet: Dexamethasone significantly reduced CSF MMP-9 concentrations in early follow up samples (median 5 days (range 3-8) of treatment), but had no significant influence on other MMPs/TIMPs.

evidence.reference_title: Genotype-stratified adjunctive dexamethasone for tuberculous meningitis in HIV-negative adults: a randomized controlled phase 3 trial.
evidence.snippet: Leukotriene A4 hydrolase (LTA4H) genotypes associate with distinct intracerebral inflammatory phenotypes and may determine corticosteroid response in tuberculous meningitis, with benefit observed in hyperinflammatory TT genotype but uncertain benefit in lower inflammation CC and CT genotypes.

nodes.description: Bacillus Calmette-Guerin vaccination in infants and young children reduces progression to disseminated meningeal or miliary tuberculosis.

evidence.reference_title: Protection by BCG vaccine against tuberculosis: a systematic review of randomized controlled trials.
evidence.snippet: Protection against meningeal and miliary tuberculosis was also high in infants (RR, 0.1; 95% CI, .01-.77) and children stringently tuberculin tested (RR, 0.08; 95% CI, .03-.25).

nodes.description: Mycobacterial antigens drive an epithelioid-macrophage-rich basal meningeal exudate around cranial nerves, basal cisterns, and cerebral vessels.

evidence.reference_title: Pathology and pathogenetic mechanisms in neurotuberculosis.
evidence.snippet: This exudate is made up of small and large mononuclear cells, including epithelioid cells, which also act as macrophages and may fuse to form Langhans' giant cells.

nodes.description: Loss of blood-brain barrier integrity during CNS tuberculosis, accompanied by inflammatory cell infiltration and reactive gliosis. Direct evidence is from a mouse CNS-TB model.

animal_models.description: Infected mice develop blood-brain barrier breakdown with MMP-9 secretion when SHH signalling is pharmacologically blocked.
animal_models.name: Mouse sonic-hedgehog CNS tuberculosis model

evidence.reference_title: Modulating sonic hedgehog (SHH) pathway to create a rapid CNS-TB model: Facilitating drug discovery.
evidence.snippet: Immunohistochemistry demonstrated that CYC caused severe BBB breakdown and reactive gliosis, while PUR partially attenuated this response.

nodes.description: Matrix metalloproteinase-9 rises in cerebrospinal fluid early in tuberculous meningitis and tracks the CSF neutrophil count.

evidence.reference_title: Dexamethasone, cerebrospinal fluid matrix metalloproteinase concentrations and clinical outcomes in tuberculous meningitis.
evidence.snippet: The strong correlation between CSF MMP-9 and neutrophil count suggests that polymorphonuclear leukocytes may play a central role in the early pathogenesis of TBM.

evidence.reference_title: Central Nervous System Tuberculosis.
evidence.snippet: The CSF formula typically shows a lymphocytic pleocytosis, and low glucose and high protein concentrations.

evidence.reference_title: Unmasking the cognitive burden of adult tuberculous meningitis: A systematic review and meta analysis.
evidence.snippet: Cognitive impairment ranging from 12% to over 90% was found across studies, with severity ranging from mild deficits to severe global dysfunction.

evidence.reference_title: Central Nervous System Tuberculosis.
evidence.snippet: TBM predominates in the western world and presents as a subacute to chronic meningitis syndrome with a prodrome of malaise, fever, and headache progressing to altered mentation and focal neurologic signs, followed by stupor, coma, and death within five to eight weeks of onset.

nodes.description: Around a quarter to a third of patients have a cranial nerve palsy. The abducens nerve is the most often affected.

evidence.reference_title: Incidence of cranial and ophthalmic nerve palsy and associated risk factors in tuberculous meningitis: A systematic review and meta-regression analysis.
evidence.snippet: The pooled prevalence of CNP in TBM patients was 26.5 % (95 % CI: 22.4-31.1 %), while ONP prevalence was 23.9 % (95 % CI: 18.7-30.0 %).

evidence.reference_title: Incidence, predictors and prognostic value of cranial nerve involvement in patients with tuberculous meningitis: a retrospective evaluation.
evidence.snippet: Abducent nerve was the most frequently (32.3%) affected cranial nerve.

evidence.reference_title: Central Nervous System Tuberculosis.
evidence.snippet: TBM predominates in the western world and presents as a subacute to chronic meningitis syndrome with a prodrome of malaise, fever, and headache progressing to altered mentation and focal neurologic signs, followed by stupor, coma, and death within five to eight weeks of onset.

nodes.description: HIV infection increases progression to active tuberculosis and CNS involvement, and TBM patients with HIV co-infection have higher mortality.

evidence.reference_title: Mortality in hospitalized patients with tuberculous meningitis.
evidence.snippet: When multivariable analysis was applied, significant associations with in-hospital mortality were seen among patients with HIV (RR 2.06; Confidence Interval 95% (95% CI) 1.44-2.94)

evidence.reference_title: Microbiological diagnosis and mortality of tuberculosis meningitis: Systematic review and meta-analysis.
evidence.snippet: the pooled case fatality rate among HIV positive and HIV negative TBM individuals was 53.39% (95%CI; 40.55-66.24) and 21.65% (95%CI;4.27-39.03) respectively.

evidence.reference_title: Central Nervous System Tuberculosis.
evidence.snippet: TBM predominates in the western world and presents as a subacute to chronic meningitis syndrome with a prodrome of malaise, fever, and headache progressing to altered mentation and focal neurologic signs, followed by stupor, coma, and death within five to eight weeks of onset.

nodes.description: Bloodborne M. tuberculosis seeds the meninges or adjacent ependymal surfaces and creates a caseating subpial or subependymal Rich focus.

evidence.reference_title: Pathology and pathogenetic mechanisms in neurotuberculosis.
evidence.snippet: The mechanisms and the changes described herein typically begin with a dense basal meningeal exudate often resulting from a "Rich focus" along the basal surface of the cerebrum or ventricular ependyma.

evidence.reference_title: Tuberculous meningitis in adults--experience from Turkey.
evidence.snippet: Hemiparesis (35.7%), cranial nerve palsy (30.9%), and altered consciousness (26.9%) were the most common neurological deficits.

evidence.reference_title: Pathology and pathogenetic mechanisms in neurotuberculosis.
evidence.snippet: Blockage of the basal subarachnoid cisterns around the midbrain and pons by the dense basal exudate or narrowing of aqueduct and third ventricle by a small tuberculoma causes consequent hydrocephalus.

nodes.description: Initial TBM therapy uses isoniazid, rifampicin, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol to kill M. tuberculosis in the CSF and cover possible resistance while susceptibility testing is pending.

evidence.reference_title: Central Nervous System Tuberculosis.
evidence.snippet: The initial 4 drug regimen (isoniazid, rifampin, pyrazinamide, ethambutol) covers the possibility of infection with a resistant strain, maximizes antimicrobial impact, and reduces the likelihood of emerging resistance on therapy.

nodes.description: Ischemic infarction downstream of tuberculous arteritis, most commonly in the basal ganglia, is a major determinant of morbidity and mortality.

evidence.reference_title: Central Nervous System Tuberculosis.
evidence.snippet: Vasculitis leading to infarcts in the basal ganglia occurs commonly and is a major determinant of morbidity and mortality.

nodes.description: Sonic-hedgehog-pathway modulation in BALB/c mice with M. tuberculosis CNS infection models MMP-9-associated blood-brain-barrier injury and rapid brain bacillary expansion.

evidence.reference_title: Modulating sonic hedgehog (SHH) pathway to create a rapid CNS-TB model: Facilitating drug discovery.
evidence.snippet: Further analysis revealed that CYC upregulated Matrix Metalloproteinase-9 (MMP-9) secretion, a key contributor to BBB disruption.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical course, complications and predictors of mortality in patients with tuberculous meningitis--an experience of fifty two cases at Civil Hospital Karachi, Pakistan.
evidence.snippet: The presenting complaints were fever 51 (98.1%), neck-stiffness 44 (84.61%), and altered level of consciousness 40 (76.9%), headache 31 (59.6%), vomiting 19 (36.5%) and focal weakness 10 (19.2%).

nodes.description: Basal exudate or tuberculoma-associated narrowing of the aqueduct and third ventricle blocks CSF pathways and causes hydrocephalus.

evidence.reference_title: Pathology and pathogenetic mechanisms in neurotuberculosis.
evidence.snippet: Blockage of the basal subarachnoid cisterns around the midbrain and pons by the dense basal exudate or narrowing of aqueduct and third ventricle by a small tuberculoma causes consequent hydrocephalus.

nodes.description: Inhaled bacilli reach alveolar macrophages and establish a pulmonary or disseminated tuberculous focus.
Rupture of the caseating Rich focus releases bacilli and mycobacterial antigens into cerebrospinal fluid and the basal subarachnoid space.

evidence.reference_title: Pathology and pathogenetic mechanisms in neurotuberculosis.
evidence.snippet: The mechanisms and the changes described herein typically begin with a dense basal meningeal exudate often resulting from a "Rich focus" along the basal surface of the cerebrum or ventricular ependyma.

evidence.reference_title: Seizures in tuberculous meningitis.
evidence.snippet: Seizures occurred in 34% patients with TBM and were associated with poor outcome at six months.

nodes.description: Basal exudate entraps large arteries and perforators, producing arteritis and arterial occlusion.

evidence.reference_title: Pathology and pathogenetic mechanisms in neurotuberculosis.
evidence.snippet: Entrapment and occasional arteritic occlusion of larger arteries, such as the middle cerebral in the Sylvian fissures, results in infarction.
